title: The Listening Harvest
premise: Beatrix Lockridge returns to the village of Hollowmere to bury her twin brother Benedict, only to learn the body in the coffin is not him—and that everyone in town already knew. When the church bell, melted down in 1911, begins ringing at dusk, Beatrix is drawn into a debt the village has carried since 1974, when their mother took something from the harvest field beneath the church: a child belonging to the land itself. To save Benedict, who is being kept 'below' as collateral, Beatrix must return what was taken—but the child has grown into something that no longer wants to go back. In the end, Beatrix offers herself in her brother's place, and the found family she never expected—the village's other marked children—refuse to let the land take her whole, sealing a new bargain: the bell will ring for them now, and they will answer it together.
about_author: Freya Marchetti grew up in a farming village on the Welsh borders where the church bell was famously silent for one year of her childhood, an absence no adult would explain. She writes horror about inheritance, small communities, and the things families bury instead of grieve.

chapters.title: The Wrong Body
chapters.summary: Beatrix arrives in Hollowmere for Benedict's funeral and finds the coffin empty except for river stones and a child's shoe. The vicar won't meet their eyes; the undertaker calls Benedict 'collected.' POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion as Beatrix realizes the village's kindness is actually containment—they are being kept here.

chapters.title: What Mother Took
chapters.summary: Searching their late mother's locked writing desk, Beatrix finds a 1974 photograph of a child standing in the harvest field, and a ledger of payments made every autumn since—to whom, it doesn't say. Old Mrs. Aldous confesses: the village gave up its own children once, until Beatrix's mother stole one back. POV: Beatrix with Mrs. Aldous interlude. Emotional beat: dread of inherited guilt.

chapters.title: The Bell That Wasn't
chapters.summary: The melted-down 1911 bell rings nightly, and each ring takes someone—first the undertaker, then the vicar, walking into the field at dusk. Beatrix descends into the flooded crypt below the church and finds Benedict alive, held by the stolen child, now grown wrong and ancient, who demands what was promised in 1974. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: terror and fierce love colliding.

chapters.title: Harvest Home
chapters.summary: Beatrix offers themself in Benedict's place, but the village's other marked children—the ones the land left behind—gather in the field and sing the old bargain back into balance: not a life owed, but a family kept. The bell rings once more and falls silent; Benedict and Beatrix stay in Hollowmere, keepers of the listening harvest. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved by choosing both.
